messages:
Sara Li: Quick update from the Navigator-11B bring-up. Ran int8 and int6 quantization sweeps on a 10k sample (mix of short Q&A and longform summarization).
Josh Patel: Nice — any surprising regressions?
Sara Li: Yes, short QA is fine across both. Longform summarization shows a small but repeatable drop in coherence at int6 for prompts >800 tokens. Example failure: repeated hallucinated date at the end.
Mei Chen: Can you paste the failure snippet?
Sara Li: "
Mei Chen: Thanks — that pattern matches the KV-cache truncation artifact we saw earlier. Might be related to the attention kernel switching when sequence >1024.
Sara Li: Agreed. We reran with forced kernel path (no switch) and int6 improves but latency worsens ~12%.
Anil Rao: What about unit econ numbers?
Sara Li: Baseline fp16 cost per 1k tokens = $0.80. int8 = $0.52 (35% savings). int6 = $0.39 (51% savings) but with quality hit on long summaries.
Elsa Gomez: Product asked what to recommend for GTN pilot — priority is user-facing summary quality, but cost is also a concern.
Josh Patel: Suggestion: hybrid routing. Use int8 for longform summarization (higher fidelity) and int6 for single-turn Q&A and embeddings where quality delta is negligible.
Mei Chen: We measured latency p95: fp16 180ms, int8 140ms, int6 125ms. So int6 is slightly faster but not dramatically.
Anil Rao: What's the expected traffic mix for GTN? Elsa?
Elsa Gomez: Early pilot estimate: 40% short Q&A, 30% multi-turn chat, 30% long summaries (>700 tokens).
Sara Li: Running a simple weighted econ: weighted cost per 1k tokens with hybrid (int6 for short, int8 for long/multi-turn) comes to ~$0.46 — ~43% savings vs fp16.
Mei Chen: Quality parity checks: sampled prompts (n=200) show int8 is within 0.95 correlation to fp16 on ROUGE and our internal coherence metric; int6 drops to ~0.88 on longform.
quant-bot: Automated eval summary: longform coherence regression flagged (p<0.01) for int6 vs fp16.
Josh Patel: Ops note — int6 artifacts are more sensitive to prompt length distribution. If product can limit summary length or enforce chunk+stitch, int6 might be acceptable.
Elsa Gomez: Product preference: keep summary quality; cost target is 30% reduction. Hybrid looks promising but we'd prefer more safety margin.
Anil Rao: Proposal: start with int8 default, route high-confidence short Qs to int6 via confidence model; run 5% canary using hybrid routing with logging and holdback.
Sara Li: Action items: (1) Mei to add kernel-path toggle to runtime and re-run 1k longform samples with forced kernel, (2) Josh to prototype hybrid routing policy & confidence classifier, (3) Elsa to sync with GTN on acceptable failure modes, (4) Anil to draft unit-econ blurb for sales (include savings scenarios).
Mei Chen: I'll run the kernel toggle + new eval by EOD tomorrow.
Josh Patel: I'll sketch routing config (flag + fallback) and a small A/B test plan.
Elsa Gomez: I'll update GTN with hybrid option and ask for target minimum coherence threshold.
Anil Rao: I'll prepare a one-pager with cost scenarios: fp16 / int8 / int6 / hybrid and include latency & quality tradeoffs.
Sara Li: FYI link to the raw spreadsheet: https://redwood.internal/sheets/nav-11b-quant-econ (biased access). Please add comments. :thumbsup:
Josh Patel: small nit — add the sample distribution column to the sheet so product sees the slice mix.
Mei Chen: Also adding a short reproducibility snippet to the sheet: `python eval.py --model navigator-11b --quant int6 --force-kernel fastattn --samples longform.json`
Sara Li: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after Mei's run.
Elsa Gomez: +1 — good plan.
quant-bot: Deploy note: canary routing rule created (rule-id: canary-nav-int6-2026)
Sara Li: Closing loop — if canary flags >1% coherence drop after 24h we rollback.
Josh Patel: I'll add the rollback monitor to the oncall dashboard.
Mei Chen: Running now, will post results.
Sara Li: End."
